spec/ui/components/scrollbar/index.pi#Scrollbar.track and

What should be true, while the board's columns are wider than the tab:
- Pressing the left button scrolls the board left a little, and the right
  button scrolls it right a little.
- Pressing the thumb and dragging left or right scrolls the board with it.
  The thumb stays under the pointer the whole way, even once the pointer
  leaves the bar, until the button is released.
- Pressing the track off the thumb centres the thumb on the press, and it
  can be dragged on from there straight away.
- Where a resize edge, such as the side panel's, overlaps the bar, a press
  goes to whichever of the two has the smaller hit area, as with the
  column.
- While the columns fit, the thumb fills the track and nothing scrolls.
- Opening and closing the side panel narrows and widens the board. The
  thumb's size and position follow the board's sideways scroll exactly,
  with no jump.

Add UI tests on Planning's board for each of these.

The prompt the chain was sent:

The board's sideways scrollbar is drawn very wrong. Once this is done, it is
the same Scrollbar as everywhere else, turned on its side, and nothing
about it is drawn as an upright column.

Read these first: spec/ui/components/scrollbar/index.pi#Scrollbar.description,
spec/ui/components/scrollbar/index.pi#Scrollbar.surface,
spec/ui/components/scrollbar/index.pi#Scrollbar.buttons,
spec/ui/components/scrollbar/index.pi#Scrollbar.track and
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.layout, which puts "the Scrollbar
along its foot". The Scrollbar spec has nothing yet on a bar along a foot.
It describes only a column along a list's right, so that part is new:
add it to the Scrollbar spec as one more way the same scrollbar is laid out.

What should be true:
- Along the board's foot is one bar, 18 pixels tall and the full width of
  the board's scrolling area. It has the same surface as what it sits on,
  and runs the board's full width whether or not anything scrolls.
- At its left end is a square button, 17 pixels wide and 18 tall, with an
  arrow pointing left. At its right end is the same button with an arrow
  pointing right. Each arrow is 6 pixels tall and 4 wide, centred up and
  down, 7 pixels in from the button's outer end, crisp on whole pixels,
  and in the same colour as the column's arrows. They lighten on hover and
  press as the column's buttons do.
- The track runs between the buttons. A one-pixel line in the raised
  colour runs along both its top and its bottom edge, into the buttons, so
  the bar reads as one raised outline. No line runs up or down across it.
- The thumb is a plain raised rectangle, the bar's full height, as wide as
  the share of the board in view and never too narrow to grab, placed as
  far along as the board is scrolled. It has a single column of pixels at
  its left and right ends in the thumb-end colour, and it lightens on hover
  and drag as the column's thumb does.
- There is no lock button and no lock gap. Nothing from an upright column
  (its width, a horizontal line across it, an up or down arrow) appears
  anywhere in the bar.
- It looks right in dark and light mode alike, on the board's surface.

Fix it in src/scrollbar.rs. Every part the column draws should be laid out
along the bar's axis, not with a fixed column width and height. Add a UI
test that captures the sideways bar and checks the points above. It should
check the bar pixel for pixel against the column's own parts turned on
their side, so the two can't drift apart again.

What the spec step said it changed, its final output:

I've fixed the board's sideways scrollbar and added the test, but I couldn't build or run anything. The build needs `.suspense/system-prompts/`, and that folder gives "permission denied" in this run, even outside the sandbox. So none of this is compiled or tested yet.

**The bug:** the bar was built as a row whose items are centred up and down, not stretched to its height. That left the track between the buttons with no height. The thumb disappeared, and the two side lines collapsed into a horizontal line across the middle of the bar. The arrows, buttons and thumb maths were already laid out sideways correctly.

**The fix, in `src/scrollbar.rs`:**
- Both the column and the bar now stretch their parts across their thickness, so the track is the bar's full 18 pixels.
- Every part is sized by two small helpers, one for its length along the scrollbar and one for its thickness across it. That covers the column/bar itself, the buttons, the track's minimum length and the lock gap, so nothing uses the column's fixed width and height any more.

**The new test, `the_bar_is_the_column_on_its_side`:** it draws a column and a bar of the same length, scrolled the same amount, side by side, in dark and then light mode. It checks:
- the bar is 18 tall and as wide as what scrolls, sits right under it, and has 17×18 buttons at each end;
- there's no lock button;
- the left and right arrows are pixel-exact, with the top and bottom lines, the thumb ends and the bare track in the right colours;
- the whole bar equals the column turned on its side, pixel for pixel, at rest, and with each button and the thumb hovered and pressed.

The spec and your request agree, so I followed both as written.

To check it once the folder is readable again, run `cargo test --bin suspense the_bar_is_the_column_on_its_side` and the other scrollbar tests.

content.text:
I added six UI tests on Planning's board, one for each point in your list, but I couldn't compile or run them. The build still fails because `.suspense/system-prompts/` is unreadable in this run, so nothing from this step or the last one has been built or tested.

I didn't change any behaviour. Reading the code, the bar's buttons, thumb drag, track press and resize-edge check already work along the bar's axis. gpui also keeps the board's scroll position in range when it widens, so the thumb shouldn't jump. The only change to `src/scrollbar.rs` is that the scroll step is now visible to the tests, plus a test-only function that says where the bar's thumb should be.

The tests, in `src/planning.rs`, find the thumb in what was actually drawn and check:
- **Buttons:** right scrolls right by one step, left scrolls back, and it stops at the left end.
- **Dragging the thumb:** the thumb stays under the pointer along the bar and above it, and pins at the right end. Nothing moves once the button is released.
- **Pressing the track:** the thumb centres on the press and follows a drag that carries on without releasing.
- **Resize edge:** an edge over the track takes the press; a button takes a press over the edge.
- **Columns fit:** the thumb fills the track, and the buttons and track press scroll nothing.
- **Side panel:** on every frame while the panel slides open and shut, the thumb matches the board's scroll. The board narrows when it opens and widens back when it closes.

Two places where the spec and your request differ:
- **No new spec text:** the spec already says pressing and dragging on the bar "work as they do on the column". The spec step added nothing about presses along a foot, so I followed that sentence.
- **No resize edge on the side panel:** the spec makes Planning's side panel a fixed 400 pixels with no resize edge. So the resize-edge test places an edge's press area over the bar itself, rather than using the side panel's.

To check everything once the folder is readable, run `cargo test --bin suspense board_` and `cargo test --bin suspense the_bar_is_the_column_on_its_side`.
